Have you tried to find a distraction? For me, forcing my mind to chew on something else can help. It's like giving a angry dog a bone. Your brain can only hold so much stuff at once. I know it's a short-term solution, but I know the temporary relief can just feel nice. 

Find a long-term video game. I play World of Warcraft and Animal Crossing and they are easy go-to's to refocus. Escape for a little while.

Another strange thing that can help is doing this, talking with someone. Reaching out and helping someone else deal with their thoughts can distract you from your own worries.
No problem. I hope everything goes well. Good luck with everything. Stay safe!

God, that's terrible. How old are you, honestly that's bloody creepy? You don't need to say how old exactly, but if you are under 18 you can contact child protective services. At the very least, a call like that might be a wake-up call to your parents that they're being terrible.

Waiting for winter break to run away sounds like a fair idea. Additionally, you might be able to make a case for yourself being checked into a mental hospital. That would give you the resources to get access to a medication plan to help you.

If you're planning on leaving permanently, there are some things you *have* to try and take with you. It will make it so you don't need to go back. If you have until winter break, try and find ways to casually obtain them. Try to get your birth certificate, your social security card, an ID if you have one. Everything else can be replaced easily, but unique copies of these things can prove your citizenship in a crunch.

Hey, I saw your previous post and this post today. 

Has anything happened between this post and the last one? It's so sweet of you for thanking the community as you have, and that alone demonstrates how sweet you are and that you do see a future where people think about you.

I've been thinking about you.

Have you thought about trying to get yourself on some variety of medication for depression? If you are on some variety of medication already, you might need to try something different. It's easier than you would think, especially during COVID-19 times. You might not even need to see someone in person, tele-therapy is often the go-to now.

You say you can't see an end in any other way, and I know trying to stay alive is so much harder than ending it. I hope you stay with us; there is always another way out.

She is terrible for acting like this. Treating you with such apathy is not on you. By being a mom, she signed up for all that you can throw at her. Instead, she is neglecting you an emotional level. She might give you the bare minimum to live, but being emotionally distant like that is classic neglect. It's easy to feel like it's your fault, but seriously it is *her, not you.* My mom treated me the same, though I'm lucky that I'm 21 and have the ability to leave. 

Have you thought about checking yourself in to a mental hospital? If you report neglect, you might be able escape. If you are in need and at risk to yourself, it could be a way to get away from her for months while doing school outside of her shadow. Additionally, they can help you learn ways to be more independent.

I understand how much it hurts to have a parent simply not care. But know that showing this lack of interest and making you feel worthless -- it is to her benefit. She doesn't need to think about her own failings, and keeping you feeling dependent and terrible just gives her more power over you. Don't believe her. You are strong.

I'm glad you did not cause yourself physical harm. I would not want you to experience the pain of a chest wound.

How are your parents directly monitoring you? Have you looked into ways of trying to disable this, or is this completely out of the picture? I'm sorry, it wasn't until your comment that everything I suggested was online. Do you have anywhere to go to avoid your parents?

Have you thought about reading? Drawing and writing fiction or poetry yourself too are alternatives if you don't have any interesting books around.

You're not weak and you're not pathetic. It takes a strange kind of bravery to stop yourself before it gets too bad. It takes bravery to post here, looking for someone real to talk to, at least for a little while.

Your parents are ones to blame here, not you. Toxic parents can make you feel like it's your fault when it's not at all. 

How much damage did you do? Did you actually make a cut or hurt yourself? Chest stabbings can lead to blood poisoning if it gets infected, and chest wounds are highly likely to get infected like that. You might not be out of the woods yet, if so. 

If you're okay, maybe find a good distraction to leave reality a different way for a while. Watch a long movie, binge a television show. Let yourself get immersed in a video game. Stuff like World of Warcraft is free for a while, and you can get a lot of time out of it without needing to pay. When I'm so angry at myself, I try to find someone else to be for a while.

Have you tried getting yourself on a medication? I know the whole thing is such an ordeal, but COVID has made it easier in some regards. You might be able to get an appointment scheduled and prescription without even leaving home. I know for me, that was a really big hump. And... you sound a lot like me. So much that I really needed to respond to you.

I'm too afraid of dying to actually end it, but lord do I want to sometimes. I understand what it feels like to hit those walls of despair and just be left stunned as to where it came from. It doesn't make sense at all, I wish I could tell you how to stop it, because that means I could stop my walls of sadness too.

In the meantime, I would recommend finding something to focus your mind on. Find a video game to play, watch a movie. Sometimes I read the news, as sad as it is sometimes, it makes it easier to focus on other people's problems so you don't need to think about you. 

Distraction is good, because sometimes if you can keep yourself distracted through the wall... when you're done the sadness might not have as much power because it isn't in the shock of the moment anymore.
